extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, higher-education and K-12 administrators, academic medical center administrators, campus legal counsel, and other recipients of Federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for how recipients of Federal financial assistance must respond to reports and formal complaints of sexual harassment under the final Title IX regulations, including procedural requirements for grievances, hearings, supportive measures, training, and scope of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient with actual knowledge of sexual harassment in an education program or activity against a person in the United States must respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to incidents involving students, employees, volunteers, and third parties when the person is participating in or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity. The Department adopts a deliberate indifference standard in §106.44(a); recipients have discretion under that standard and under §106.44(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures irrespective of filing a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to a complainant regardless of whether the complainant files a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures may include changes to schedules, assignments (e.g., assigning a patient to a different physician), separate rooms during hearings, changes to clinical clerkship placements, and other non-disciplinary supports. Supportive measures must be available even if the recipient dismisses a formal complaint for insufficient evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents (§106.44(a) and §106.45(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must treat complainants and respondents equitably: offer supportive measures to complainants and provide a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before imposing disciplinary sanctions or other non-supportive measures on respondents; provide remedies where a respondent is found responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule distinguishes equitable treatment from identical/equal treatment; equity may require different procedural steps given differing circumstances. Revisions to §106.44(a) and §106.45(b)(1)(i) implement this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing with cross-examination for postsecondary institutions (§106.45(b)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions must provide a live hearing in which a party's advisor may conduct cross-examination of the other party and witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may be located in separate rooms during the live hearing; concerns about resource burdens and power differentials were considered, but the Department requires the live hearing for postsecondary institutions. Hearing advisors who conduct cross-examination should be competent and qualified; recipients must ensure training and manage conflicts/bias as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative written question process for non-postsecondary recipients (§106.45(b)(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For recipients that are not postsecondary institutions, the grievance process may not require a live hearing but must at minimum afford each party the opportunity to submit written questions, provide each party with the answers, and allow for additional limited follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision provides flexibility for contexts like academic medical centers, clinical settings, or off‑site preceptorships where live hearings may be unworkable. Recipients still must ensure parties have an opportunity to challenge and respond to evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasonably prompt time frames for filing and resolving grievances (§106.45(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include reasonably prompt time frames for the conclusion of the grievance process, including reasonably prompt time frames for filing and resolving appeals and for informal resolution processes if offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable promptness applies to all phases of the grievance process; recipients must balance speed with procedural fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and impartiality of Title IX personnel (§106.45(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train Title IX personnel (including hearing officers) on the scope of the recipient's education program or activity and ensure personnel are free from conflicts of interest and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officers may be faculty members provided they are trained, do not have conflicts of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents, and comply with §106.45(b)(1)(iii). Training must include understanding the recipient's program/activity scope and relevant procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution limitations (no informal resolution when an employee sexually harasses a student)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer informal resolution to resolve allegations between two employees under §106.45(b)(9), but may not offer or facilitate informal resolution for allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction reflects concern about power dynamics and potential coercion of students; recipients retain discretion to offer informal resolution in other employee-on-employee matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal when evidence cannot be gathered (§106.45(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a formal complaint if specific circumstances prevent the recipient from gathering evidence sufficient to reach a determination as to the formal complaint or allegations therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a complaint is dismissed for insufficient evidence, the recipient must still offer supportive measures to complainants under §106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: 'education program or activity' includes locations/events where recipient exercised substantial control (§106.44(a), 34 CFR 106.2(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Education program or activity includes locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department will interpret program/activity consistent with Title IX statutory and regulatory definitions and Supreme Court guidance in Davis; recipients must assess whether off‑site clerkships, affiliates, or clinical settings are within their program/activity based on control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to employees, volunteers, third parties, and dual-role persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX and the final regulations apply to any person in the United States who experiences sex discrimination in an education program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance — including employees, volunteers, third parties, and students who are also employees, subject to factual determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider facts of each incident to decide applicability; volunteers may be covered if they experience discrimination in the recipient's program/activity; third parties may file complaints but may be less likely to participate in grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients retain discretion on faculty governance involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may involve existing faculty-governance committees in Title IX processes (e.g., referrals for faculty respondents) but the Department will not mandate creation of such committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where used, faculty hearing officers must meet the training, conflict, and bias requirements. The Department defers to recipient discretion on how to incorporate shared governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-system coordination: Title IX does not supplant Title VII and Department won't opine on Title VII obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: These final Title IX regulations do not override statutory rights under Title VII; the Department will not issue regulations or opine on an employer's obligations under Title VII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes different standards may apply under Title VII (e.g., employer liability standards) and will construe Title IX to avoid actual conflict with Title VII; courts decide private rights of action and interplay between Title IX and Title VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materially false statements in bad faith may be sanctioned without constituting retaliation (§106.71(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposing sanctions for making a materially false statement in bad faith in the course of a grievance proceeding does not constitute retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient considering sanctions for false statements must examine the content, purpose, intent, and circumstances to determine whether the statement constitutes sex discrimination; materially false statements may but do not always constitute discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must provide remedies when respondent found responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: When a respondent is found responsible, recipients must provide remedies to the complainant as part of equitable treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies are required by §106.45(b)(1)(i) revisions and are distinct from supportive measures; they flow from a responsibility determination and aim to restore or preserve access to the education program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for ensuring advisors/hearing personnel are competent and qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are responsible for ensuring those overseeing hearings and those conducting cross-examination (e.g., advisors) are competent and qualified to perform those roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised concerns about resource imbalances (employees hiring skilled attorneys vs students); Department notes resources vary and recipients must ensure fairness, training, and impartiality of personnel rather than assume counsel availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients remain free to decline Federal funds to avoid Title IX coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may choose not to receive Federal financial assistance and thus not become subject to these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an acknowledgment of recipient choice rather than a compliance mechanism; recipients that accept Federal funds are bound by Title IX obligations.
